## v0.13.0

### Added
- **`make demo`: from a checkout to a finished run in one command.** It builds the images, creates a
  kind (or `CLUSTER_TOOL=minikube`) cluster, installs from `deploy/`, and runs the story-writer
  example, printing the agent's output. With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set the run is real; without it a
  mock agent stands in, so it needs no key. `EXAMPLES=all` runs every example. CI now runs
  `make itest-examples` (every example schema-checked and run, mocked) on changes to `examples/`,
  `deploy/` or `packages/`, so a broken example fails the build. `examples/run-agent.sh` honours
  `KUBE_CONTEXT` to target a context other than the current one.
- **Isolating runs with gVisor or Kata is documented and tested.** A Station's
  `template.spec.runtimeClassName` already reached every run pod; a unit test now pins that, the new
  *Isolate runs* guide covers setting it up (and what the controller enforces regardless), and
  `examples/station-gvisor.yaml` is a ready Station.
- **Realtime sessions: an agent CLI that stays up and takes prompts over HTTP.** An AgentDefinition
  with `execution: realtime` starts its run as usual, with the rendered prompt as the first turn, then
  keeps the session open. Callers send more prompts with
  `POST /v1/namespaces/<ns>/agents/<name>/prompt` (`{"prompt":"…"}`, answered 202 with the turn
  number and session id) and end it with `POST …/close`, through the controller's new prompt API
  (port 8082, Service `agent-controller-api`, bearer token from the `agent-realtime` Secret). The
  controller forwards each request to the run pod's supervisor on port 8090. Claude runs one process
  fed turns on stdin; Codex and Gemini run one process per turn, resuming the session; opencode and
  `exec` start every turn fresh and raise a `no-continuity` warning. Turns run one at a time, at most
  16 queued, and each raises `{"kind":"turn",…}` events. The session ends, saves its conversation
  under its session id and goes `Succeeded` when it is closed, receives no prompt for
  `realtime.idleTimeoutMinutes` (default 15), or is signalled; the Station's `deadlineMinutes` stays the
  hard limit. The save needs `resources.conversation.source` and a vendor that keeps state.
  `status.sessionId` is recorded as soon as a prompt's reply reveals it (for a fresh Codex or Gemini
  session, from the second prompt on, since the first turn announces it), and an Agent with
  `spec.resumeSession: <id>` restores that conversation from `resources.conversation.source` and waits
  for prompts without sending the definition's prompt. Realtime is opt-in through the
  `deploy/components/realtime` kustomize component, which also adds a NetworkPolicy letting only
  controller pods reach port 8090 of realtime run pods.

- **Runs report their agent session id.** The supervisor raises a `{"kind":"session","id":…}` event
  when the agent's stream announces its session (Claude `system`/`init`, Codex `thread.started`,
  Gemini `init`), and again right before the final `agent` lifecycle event. The controller records
  the last one as `status.sessionId` when the run ends. `@re-cinq/agent-contracts` adds
  `AgentStatus.sessionId`.

- **A `ModelCatalog` resource lists the models the subsystem can run.** The controller keeps one
  object, `default` (short name `mc`), in its namespace. It collects the `agent-secrets` keys that
  AgentDefinitions map as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`, calls each
  vendor's list-models API with them, and writes `status.vendors[]`: the `vendor` CLI and `provider`,
  the `secretRefs` queried, an `error` for keys that failed, and the `models` (`id`, `displayName`)
  the subsystem would route to that vendor. It refreshes when a replica becomes leader and then every
  `MODEL_CATALOG_REFRESH_SECONDS` (default 3600). The catalog is opt-in through the
  `deploy/components/model-catalog` kustomize component, which grants the controller `get` on the
  `agent-secrets` Secret and sets `MODEL_CATALOG_ENABLED=true`. The caller role can `get`, `list` and
  `watch` `modelcatalogs`, and `@re-cinq/agent-contracts` adds `AgentContractsClient.getModelCatalog()` with the
  `ModelCatalog`, `ModelCatalogStatus`, `VendorModels` and `ModelInfo` types. AgentDefinition models
  are not checked against the catalog. New reference page: *ModelCatalog CRD*.

- **`execution: batch` works for OpenAI models through the OpenAI Batch API.** A batch definition
  whose model routes to Codex (`gpt-*`, `o1`/`o3`/`o4*`, `*codex*`, for example `gpt-5-mini`) is
  submitted by the controller as a one-line JSONL file of `POST /v1/responses` calls (`/v1/files`,
  then `/v1/batches`) with the `OPENAI_API_KEY` entry of `resources.secrets`, shows
  `status.batchProvider: openai`, and is polled and cancelled like the other batches; cleanup
  deletes the batch's input, output and error files, since OpenAI batch objects cannot be deleted,
  treating a file already gone as deleted. A response that only refuses fails the run with the
  refusal text. Cleanup of an OpenAI or Anthropic batch now waits for a cancel to settle (the batch
  stays `cancelling`/`canceling` for minutes) instead of running right after it, keeping the
  `agents.re-cinq.com/batch-cleanup` finalizer meanwhile without counting failed attempts, up to 48
  hours after `startedAt`; before, a deleted or timed-out Anthropic batch's cleanup failed and an
  OpenAI batch's late output file was left behind.
  `status.output` and the sinks get the codex CLI's `exec --json` lines for a single-turn run
  (`thread.started`, `turn.started`, an `agent_message` item and `turn.completed` with `usage`, or
  `error` and `turn.failed`); there is no cost field, as the CLI has none. An `output.schema` is
  sent as a strict `json_schema` `text.format`. The Floor parses no codex events yet, so a codex
  run's text and usage do not reach it, CLI or batch. Opencode models are still rejected. The
  controller needs HTTPS egress to `api.openai.com` for OpenAI batch runs.
- **`execution: batch` works for Gemini models through the Gemini Batch API.** A batch definition
  whose model routes to Gemini (for example `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) is submitted by the controller
  to `models/<model>:batchGenerateContent` with the `GEMINI_API_KEY` entry of `resources.secrets`,
  shows `status.batchProvider: gemini`, and is polled, cancelled and deleted like an Anthropic batch.
  `status.output` and the sinks get the gemini CLI's `stream-json` lines for a single-turn run
  (`init`, an assistant `message`, and a `result` with `status` and `stats`), so a consumer reads it
  like a gemini CLI run; there is no cost field, as the CLI has none. An `output.schema` is sent as
  `generationConfig.responseJsonSchema`. Opencode models are still rejected. The
  controller needs HTTPS egress to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` for Gemini batch runs.
  A batch poll that errors is logged and retried until the batch timeout, which still fails the
  Agent or falls back to a Job.
- **`mcp_servers` take any number of secret-backed `headers` (http/sse) and `env` vars (stdio).**
  Each is `{name, ref}` with `ref` an `agent-secrets` key, injected as `MCP_<SERVER>_<NAME>` and
  referenced by every CLI, so servers that want `X-API-Key`, several headers, or a token in a
  stdio process's environment work without anyone logging in.
- **`resources.mcp_servers` now reach Codex and OpenCode runs**, not only Claude and Gemini.
  Codex gets them as `-c mcp_servers.<name>.…` overrides, OpenCode as the `mcp` key of its
  global config; `headers_secret` is referenced from the pod env as for the other CLIs, so the
  token never reaches argv or disk. New guide: *Connect MCP servers*.
- **An AgentDefinition can run as a provider batch request: `execution: batch`.** For Claude
  models the controller submits the rendered prompt to the Anthropic Message Batches API itself,
  at about half the price of the regular API, with no Job or pod. It polls the batch every
  `BATCH_POLL_SECONDS` (default 60) and writes the result to `status.output` as the same Claude CLI
  `stream-json` lines a single-turn run prints. `status.batchId`, `batchProvider`, `batchFallback`
  and `batchCleanupAttempts` record the batch. `batch.timeoutMinutes` (default 1440) bounds the wait;
  `batch.onTimeout: fail` fails the Agent with `batch timed out`, `fallback` cancels the batch and
  runs the same definition as a normal Job at full price. A batch is one model call, so a batch
  definition that sets tools, `max_turns`, repos, MCP servers, skills, a conversation,
  `output.watch`, the `exec` model or an opencode model, or an Agent that sets `spec.files`, fails the Agent with the
  field named. An `output.schema` is sent as structured output (`output_config.format` of type
  `json_schema`). `batch.maxTokens` (default 16000) sets the request's `max_tokens`, and a run with no
  model anywhere uses `claude-opus-5-5`. The `result` event's `total_cost_usd` is half the model's
  standard price for the reported tokens (Anthropic list prices as of 2026-10, exact model id match;
  `0` for a model not in the table), `usage` passes through cache token counts when present, and
  `thinking` blocks are dropped so the events read like the CLI's. An Agent's `spec.model` overrides the definition's model for the
  request and the model check, as it does for a Job. Under `concurrencyPolicy: Replace` a new batch
  Agent preempts the oldest run and submits its batch. The controller delivers the run's events to the
  definition's `output.sinks` in the usual envelope (no `pod` in `source`): `agent`/`started` on
  submit, the CLI lines through `output.select` and `agent`/`succeeded` or `agent`/`failed`
  (`reason: batch_failed`) when the batch ends, and a `batch_timeout` lifecycle event on a timeout
  (`failed` for `onTimeout: fail`, `running` for `fallback`). Each is sent after its status patch, at
  most once, and an http sink's `headers_secret` is read from `agent-secrets`. The `result` event
  carries `modelUsage` like the CLI's. Deleting an in-flight batch Agent cancels and
  deletes its batch through the `agents.re-cinq.com/batch-cleanup` finalizer;
  `controller_batch_cleanup_failures_total` on `/metrics` counts failed provider cleanups.

### Changed
- **Codex CLI pinned to 0.142.5.** A Codex run used to install whatever `chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh`
  called latest, so a CLI change such as 0.142 no longer reading `OPENAI_API_KEY` reached run pods
  without notice. The init now downloads the 0.142.5 `codex-package-<arch>-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`
  from the openai/codex GitHub release for `x86_64` or `aarch64`, checks its SHA-256 against the
  pinned value before unpacking, and links `codex` into `$HOME/.local/bin` as the installer did. A
  package with a different checksum, or any other architecture, fails the init. The init now also
  needs `sha256sum`, and installs `coreutils` if the base image lacks it. The version is the
  `codexCliVersion` constant, raised on purpose.
- **The Notification API documents a consumer contract for Claude, Gemini and Codex runs.** The
  reference lists, per vendor, the fields with their JSON types that both CLI and batch runs emit
  (Claude's `result` and `system` init, Gemini's `init`, `message` and `result`, Codex's turn and
  `agent_message` lines) and the lifecycle fields every vendor emits; the unit tests check it against
  recorded CLI runs and recorded batch results.
- **Batch execution is opt-in through the `deploy/components/batch` kustomize component.** It adds
  a Role with `get` on the `agent-secrets` Secret (that Secret only) and sets `BATCH_ENABLED=true` on
  the controller, which then reads the provider API key itself. The default install, including the
  release `install.yaml`, keeps the controller without any Secret access, and a batch Agent there
  fails with `batch execution is disabled on this controller`. Enable it with
  `components: [<deploy>/components/batch]` in your kustomization. If your cluster restricts egress
  from the controller, allow HTTPS to `api.anthropic.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and
  `api.openai.com` for batch runs. Disabling batch with
  runs in flight fails those Agents with the same reason and an `agent`/`failed` sink event, and
  releases their `batch-cleanup` finalizer; their provider batches are left to finish and expire,
  and are still billed.

### Deprecated
- `mcp_servers[].headers_secret`: use `headers: [{name: Authorization, ref: <key>}]`. It keeps
  working unchanged.

### Fixed
- **`examples/run-agent.sh` with more than one `key=value` produced invalid YAML.** Each parameter
  lost its newline, so the documented bug-fixer command failed with `did not find expected key`.
  The new examples CI job caught it.
- **The init can download over https on a bare Debian or Ubuntu image.** When curl was
  missing, the init installed it with `apt-get install --no-install-recommends`, which skips
  `ca-certificates`. Every https download after that, from agent CLI installs to skills and input
  files, then failed with `curl: (77) error setting certificate file`. The init now installs
  `ca-certificates` with curl through apt, dnf and apk.
- **A failed gemini-cli download fails the init.** The Gemini install step ran its commands
  inside `command -v gemini || { … }`, where bash ignores `set -e`, so only the final `chmod`
  decided its exit status: a download or extract error still reported success and left a
  `gemini` wrapper pointing at a missing bundle, and the run failed later with a less clear
  error. The step now stops at the first failing command.
- **Release binaries are linked with lld, so their thread-locals can no longer alias.** The
  controller, `ai-agent-init` and `ai-agent-supervisor` in the published images were linked by
  the Rocky 9 builder's ld.bfd (binutils 2.35), which predates `SHF_GNU_RETAIN`: whenever LDC marks
  a `.tbss` section retained, it emits a second `.tbss` at the same address and two thread-local
  variables share storage, corrupting state in ways that depend on the build (a CI build of the
  supervisor lost all agent output this way). The images and the portable `ai-agent-init` build
  now link with lld, and the build fails if a binary has more than one `.tbss`
  (`scripts/check-tbss.sh`).
- **Codex runs now authenticate with an `OPENAI_API_KEY` key.** Current `codex exec` reads
  its key only from `CODEX_API_KEY` and sends no bearer at all (`401 Missing bearer`) when a
  definition mapped the key as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. A Codex run with an `OPENAI_API_KEY` entry in
  `resources.secrets` or `resources.env` and no `CODEX_API_KEY` of its own now also gets
  `CODEX_API_KEY` with the same value: a second `secretKeyRef` to the same `agent-secrets` key for
  a secret, the same literal for an env entry. Either name works; other vendors are unchanged.
- **A codex run that ends in `turn.failed` is reported `Failed` as soon as that line arrives.** The
  supervisor took only `turn.completed` as codex's final event, so a codex CLI that lingered after a
  failed turn kept the Job running until its deadline.
- **A gemini run whose `result` line says `"status":"error"` no longer reports success when the
  CLI has to be stopped after it.** The supervisor read a gemini `result` like a Claude one and,
  finding no `is_error`, took every gemini result as a success; when the CLI then lingered and was
  signalled, the Agent was reported `Succeeded`. It now reads `status`.
- **Invalid `resources.mcp_servers` now fail the Agent instead of being silently dropped.** An
  `exec` definition with MCP servers, a duplicate or empty server name, an `http`/`sse` server
  without `url`, a `stdio` server without `command`, a name other than letters, digits, `_`
  and `-`, or `sse` on Codex moves the Agent to `Failed` with the
  reason in `status.failureReason`, and no Job is created.

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
  # A new advisory lands on an unchanged tree, and the repository can go days without a push. Monday 07:00 UTC;
  # only build-chain answers it (#202).
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      # Both re:cinq libraries install from the npm registry, whose tarballs ship
      # built code, so no dependency needs a lifecycle script.
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # The api tests run against a real mongod, ~100MB that would otherwise be
      # downloaded again on every run. Keyed on the pinned version.
      - name: Cache the mongod the api tests start
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/mongodb-binaries
          key: mongod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('apps/api/test/mongoTestServer.ts') }}

      # A git or file dependency skips the registry the published libraries exist to prove (#13).
      - name: Keep dependency specifiers on the npm registry
        run: npm run check:dependencies

      # The engine's package root pulls every provider SDK into the browser, and booking data must never touch storage.
      # A test file ships in no bundle, so it may import the engine's recordedFrames; shipped code never does.
      - name: Keep HAL Engine and browser storage out of the web app
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"]@re-cinq/hal-engine|import\(['\"]@re-cinq/hal-engine" apps/web/src --exclude='*.test.ts' --exclude='*.test.tsx'; then
            echo "shipped apps/web code must not import @re-cinq/hal-engine" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if jq -e '.dependencies["@re-cinq/hal-engine"]' apps/web/package.json > /dev/null; then
            echo "apps/web may list @re-cinq/hal-engine under devDependencies only" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -rnE "localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|fetch\(|sendBeacon" apps/web/src/chat apps/web/src/screens apps/web/src/personas; then
            echo "apps/web chat code must not touch browser storage or send anything but the socket" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The model allowlist gates what configuration/ reads; a second reader would bypass it.
      - name: Read model, region and provider settings only in the api configuration
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "process\.env" apps packages --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist \
            | grep -E "MODEL|REGION|LOCATION|PROVIDER" | grep -v '^apps/api/src/configuration/'; then
            echo "only apps/api/src/configuration/ may read a model, region or provider value from process.env" >&2
            exit 1

  spawner needs `schedule`, `github` or both. Opt in with the `deploy/components/webhooks` component

  and controller-runtime. A small `Client` mirrors the TS one: `CreateAgent`, `GetAgent`,
  `FindAgents`, `WaitForAgent`, `GetModelCatalog`, `ApplyAgentDefinition` and `ApplyStation`.
  Fields the schema defaults are pointers, so an unset field keeps the server's default. `make drift`

  `packages/agent-contracts-go/vX.Y.Z`. The CRD type list lives in one place
  (`agentcore.crds.registry`), read by crdgen and both emitters.

  Agent in `spec.stationRef` with `spec.parameters` on a five-field UTC cron `spec.schedule` (`*`,
  numbers, ranges, steps and lists; Sunday is 0 or 7). `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` skips a tick while
  an Agent it created is still `Pending` or `Running`; `suspend: true` pauses it. The leader checks
  spawners every 15 seconds and records the slot in `status.lastScheduleTime` and `status.lastAgent`,

  for the latest missed slot. Spawned Agents are named `<spawner>-<slot minute>`, labelled

  `examples/nightly-story.yaml`.

  `delivery.pullRequest` (`base`, `titleTemplate` rendered from the Agent's parameters, `draft`,
  `apiUrl`) delivers a successful run's commits as a GitHub pull request and records its URL in
  `status.prUrl`, which nothing wrote before. The agent container then gets no repo token, no
  `GH_TOKEN` and no `AGENT_GIT_CREDENTIAL`/`AGENT_GIT_CREDENTIAL_URL`, and the init clones without
  persisting a credential helper, token file or auth header into the clone. When the agent exits, the
  supervisor writes a `git bundle` of the clone's `HEAD` to a shared `outbox` volume. A new `courier`
  container (`ai-agent-init courier`, from the agent image) holds the token, pushes the bundle to
  `refs/heads/<branch>` (the Agent's `branch`, default `agent/<name>`), opens the pull request on the
  Agent's `targetRepo` or the repo's own `owner/name` (reusing one already open from that branch), and

  only. A failed push or API call fails the run with `failureReason: pull request delivery failed: …`.

  and `PullRequestDelivery`. New task page: *Open pull requests*.

  oci://ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts/ai-agent-subsystem --version <version> --namespace default` installs

  `controller.image.digest` and `agentImage` (digest-pinned only; tags are rejected by the values
  schema) and the toggles `batch.enabled`, `modelCatalog.enabled` and `realtime.enabled`, which match

  Kustomize stays the source of truth (ADR-004): `scripts/check-helm-drift.sh`, now part of
  `make drift`, fails when the chart and `deploy/` render different objects.

- **The CRDs are now `agents.re-cinq.com/v1beta1`.** Objects are stored at `v1beta1`, and the
  controller, the generated contracts and every example and doc use it. Nothing needs converting:
  `v1alpha1` is still served with the same schema. The group and version are defined once
  (`agentcore.crds.api_group`), and crdgen, tsgen, the controller's API paths and Job owner
  references all read them from there. `@re-cinq/agent-contracts` now exports `GROUP` and
  `VERSION` from its generated types, and `VERSION` is `"v1beta1"`.

### Deprecated
- **`agents.re-cinq.com/v1alpha1`** is still served, but the API server answers each request for
  it with a deprecation warning. It won't be removed before `v1`. The install guide's *API versions
  and upgrading* section shows how to rewrite existing objects so they are stored at `v1beta1`.

### Fixed
- **The release pin step no longer breaks the realtime guide's release URLs.** Its `?ref=` rewrite
  matched `v\S+`, which swallowed the closing backtick and comma after the version, so v0.13.0's
  *Realtime sessions* page rendered both component URLs as broken code spans. It now matches only
  the version, and the page is repaired.

The knowledge graph, episode ingestion, and temporal facts shipped recently. That was the biggest pending item from a month ago. The nightly context quality evaluator, the weekly autoresearch loop, and spec drift detection are all running.

Still pending: a local read cache so developer installs don't hit the remote API on every read query, and retrieval latency optimization. We're tracking p50/p95/p99 per MCP tool in the analytics dashboard but haven't started tuning yet.

The hard problems we haven't solved: when parallel Jobs touch the same files, merging their output is manual. Sonnet implementation tasks cost real money and we're still figuring out the right task-to-model mapping. And the autoresearch loop exists but tuning the PromptFoo eval suites, deciding what "good context" actually means, is ongoing.
